rules.name: The higher timeframe sets the directional bias and lower timeframes should not override it on their own
rules.setupAnchor: Start from the higher timeframe and classify it as expansion higher, expansion lower, or consolidation before looking for lower-timeframe entries
rules.confirmationTrigger: Only keep lower-timeframe directional ideas that agree with the higher-timeframe bias or phase read
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: Lower-timeframe protected swings are only high quality when they develop in the same direction as the higher-timeframe intent
rules.invalidationCondition: A lower-timeframe pattern is traded as standalone direction even though the higher timeframe is clearly framed the other way or still consolidating
rules.targetLogic: Use the higher timeframe to choose the directional objective, then let lower timeframes optimize entry rather than redefine the thesis
exceptions: Countertrend lower-timeframe moves can still occur, but they should be treated as retracements or lower-confidence exceptions rather than default trade direction
machineChecks: Require a higher-timeframe directional classification before evaluating lower-timeframe entries
Reject lower-timeframe continuation signals that directly oppose the higher-timeframe bias
Downgrade all lower-timeframe setups when the higher timeframe is still unresolved consolidation

rules.name: The intermediate timeframe must confirm the higher-timeframe bias with structure, a point of interest, and a directional closure
rules.setupAnchor: After the higher timeframe sets direction, drop to the intermediate timeframe to map the point of interest and local structure
rules.confirmationTrigger: Require an intermediate-timeframe reaction, candle closure, or CISD in the point of interest that agrees with the higher-timeframe bias
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: The intermediate timeframe is where new protected swings begin to validate that the higher-timeframe idea is expressing itself structurally
rules.invalidationCondition: The intermediate timeframe never confirms at the point of interest or prints structure against the higher-timeframe bias
rules.targetLogic: Use the intermediate timeframe to turn the higher-timeframe directional idea into a tradeable structure before refining entry further
exceptions: A very clean higher-timeframe setup can sometimes be traded directly from the intermediate timeframe without a deeper lower-timeframe drill-down
machineChecks: Require an intermediate-timeframe point of interest that agrees with higher-timeframe direction
Require a directional closure or CISD before promoting the setup to execution-ready state
Flag the setup as pending when higher-timeframe bias exists but intermediate-timeframe structure is still missing
ambiguityNotes: The strict first-pass proxy for CISD still needs a cleaner algorithm than the current narrative description

rules.name: The lower timeframe is for entry precision only after the higher and intermediate timeframes are already aligned
rules.setupAnchor: Move to the lower timeframe only after the higher timeframe bias and intermediate-timeframe structure are pointing in the same direction
rules.confirmationTrigger: Accept the lower-timeframe entry when it confirms the aligned direction through a protected swing, continuation order block, or similar structure event
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: The lower timeframe contributes execution-quality protected swings after alignment, not before it
rules.invalidationCondition: The lower timeframe is used to force a trade before the higher and intermediate layers agree, or its structure immediately fails against the aligned direction
rules.targetLogic: Use the lower timeframe to improve risk-to-reward and timing while the higher layers continue to define the main target
exceptions: If the structure timeframe already gives a clean entry, a lower-timeframe refinement is optional rather than mandatory
pineInputsNeeded: alignment flag between higher and intermediate timeframes
machineChecks: Gate lower-timeframe entry logic behind an explicit higher-plus-intermediate alignment flag
Treat lower-timeframe structure as execution refinement instead of independent direction selection
Invalidate the refined entry when lower-timeframe structure immediately breaks against the aligned thesis

rules.name: A clean trend requires aligned expansion-supporting candles across at least two timeframes
rules.setupAnchor: Check whether the parent candles across the active timeframe stack all support expansion with small opposing wicks and directional closes
rules.confirmationTrigger: Treat the trend as clean when at least two timeframes support expansion in the same direction; treat three aligned timeframes as the ideal trend case
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: Protected swings are more likely to extend cleanly when the parent candles above them are all aligned for expansion
rules.invalidationCondition: One of the parent candles prints a large opposing wick or otherwise fails to support expansion, breaking the alignment stack
rules.targetLogic: Press continuation expectations when multiple timeframes are aligned and reduce expectations when one of the parent candles stops supporting expansion
exceptions: A single lower-timeframe trend can still occur without full stack alignment, but it should be treated as weaker than the multi-timeframe version
machineChecks: Require at least two expansion-supporting timeframe flags for the clean-trend classification
Elevate the setup quality when all three monitored timeframes align
Downgrade or defer the setup when any parent timeframe prints a non-expansion-supporting candle
ambiguityNotes: The first strict numeric rule for what makes a candle expansion-supporting still depends on the wick-logic thresholds

openQuestions: What is the best first explicit proxy for CISD so intermediate-timeframe confirmation can be scored without discretionary chart reading?
How many alignment failures across the stack should immediately cancel a setup instead of merely downgrading it?
